historical_timeline.summary: Wounded by a mortar shell near Fossalta di Piave while serving with a volunteer ambulance unit in Italy; long hospital stay.
Made his home at Finca Vigía outside Havana, where he lived until 1960.
Two plane crashes in Uganda on consecutive days: concussion, skull fracture and internal injuries.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature; unable to attend the ceremony because of ill health.
Admitted to the Mayo Clinic for severe depression and treated with electroconvulsive therapy; readmitted after a relapse in April 1961; complained afterwards that his memory was damaged.
Died by suicide at his home in Ketchum, Idaho.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Several conditions that make each other worse, met in one man without judgment: a 55-year-old writer with severe alcohol use disorder, a year after a concussion with a skull fracture, whose routine intake tests show iron overload. The episode covers the diagnosis of hereditary hemochromatosis by transferrin saturation, ferritin and HFE genotyping; staging the liver with elastography and MRI instead of biopsy (AASLD 1940, ACG 1948); weekly phlebotomy to a ferritin of 50 to 100 ng/mL; avoiding iron and vitamin C supplements and raw shellfish; why alcohol multiplies the liver risk of iron overload; offering testing to first-degree relatives without attributing results to anyone; the AUDIT, DSM-5-TR criteria, brief intervention and naltrexone, with the patient choosing his own drinking goal (APA 1947); depression treated with psychotherapy and a carefully chosen SSRI (VA/DoD 1951); a structured suicide-risk assessment with respectful lethal-means counseling about firearms and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (VA/DoD 1953); post-concussion symptoms managed by symptom (VA/DoD 1950) with cognitive screening and no diagnosis of chronic traumatic encephalopathy, which can be confirmed only after death; hypertension (CMID, ACC/AHA 1946); and diabetes screening.

assessment.assessment: C282Y homozygosity with a transferrin saturation over 45% and a raised ferritin confirms HFE hemochromatosis. Alcohol raises ferritin and adds liver injury, but with this genotype and a saturation of 76% most of the iron excess is genetic; the liver iron concentration on MRI will show the size of the load. His heavy drinking multiplies the risk of cirrhosis from iron

A ferritin over 1,000 ng/mL with a raised ALT means a higher risk of advanced fibrosis, so staging is needed. Today's stiffness of 9.4 kPa is indeterminate and may be raised by recent drinking and inflammation. An MRI with R2* liver iron quantification and magnetic resonance elastography can stage the liver without a biopsy, as the ACG guideline allows; a biopsy would be considered only if the MRI suggested advanced fibrosis or another cause

Naltrexone is reasonable: his aminotransferases are under three times the upper limit, he has no acute hepatitis or liver failure, and his liver tests have already fallen. Repeat them at about one month and then every few months. For his liver the safest amount of alcohol is none, at least while iron is being removed; he has chosen to keep cutting down first, and that choice should be respected and revisited

He should avoid iron and vitamin C supplements and raw shellfish, because iron overload greatly raises the risk of severe Vibrio infection; ordinary food needs no iron restriction

clinical_review.notes: Awaiting clinician review; check naltrexone with raised aminotransferases, the choice of sertraline, the drinking goal and the gradual reduction without medicine for withdrawal, noninvasive staging instead of biopsy with a ferritin over 1,000 ng/mL, the phlebotomy schedule and target, the post-concussion plan without imaging, and the lethal-means counseling.

provenance_review.notes: Sources: NobelPrize.org (three pages), a 2022 review in Arquivos de Neuro-Psiquiatria, PBS NewsHour, Hektoen International, Psychiatric Times (interview with Andrew Farah), Smithsonian Magazine, the Fresh Air archive and WBUR. The biographies and Hemingway's Brain were not read. Hemochromatosis and bipolar disorder are graded R and disputed; chronic traumatic encephalopathy is R and possible.

safe_messaging_review.notes: Mental health and alcohol claims are marked sensitive; his death and his father's are recorded once each in one plain sentence without method; family deaths are recorded without names or detail; the safety assessment gives the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and addresses firearms respectfully.
